title: Safety warnings lose force when proof burden flips under schedule, production, certification, or metric pressure
summary: This pattern candidate names a recurring structure: evidence of danger exists before the event, but it is not converted into authoritative action. The signal may be normalized, contained locally, classified as not safety-of-flight, treated as needing proof of unsafety, weakened by schedule/production pressure, masked by misleading metrics, or assumed away by certification models. Rev0006 supports the candidate with four official-source-backed records but refuses to treat it as a mature theory.

status_history.note: Seed/candidate queue listed production pressure overriding safety as a cross-engineering pattern.
Promoted using Challenger, Columbia, Boeing 737 MAX, and BP Texas City records.

place.scope: cross-domain: spaceflight, commercial aviation, chemical/process safety

claims.claim: Challenger, Columbia, Boeing 737 MAX, and BP Texas City are sufficient to promote MKH-PAT-0002 from seed mention to source-backed pattern candidate: warning signals existed but lost force before becoming authoritative action under schedule, production, certification, or metric pressure.
what_would_change_status: A second review demotes one or more cases, or negative controls show the pattern is too broad without narrower subfamilies.

claims.claim: The warning-governance record structure needs fields for signal, landing zone, authority, proof burden, response, outcome, and post-incident recommendation, because final-cause summaries alone hide why warning knowledge failed to change action.
what_would_change_status: Later records show these fields are redundant or miss the key causal units.

limitations: Cases are severe high-profile failures, so survivorship/selection bias is strong.
Pattern may need subfamilies: launch decision, mission management, certification assumption, process-safety metric trap.
evidence_profile.red_team_state: rev0016 scaffold added; controls not yet promoted

type_payload.candidate_mechanism: A warning signal is present but does not become binding action because its authority is weaker than schedule, production, certification, or metric structures; in some cases the burden shifts to engineers/operators to prove danger rather than to management/system owners to prove safety.

case_support.signal: O-ring erosion, low-temperature concern, Thiokol engineering objections
case_support.failure_mode: signal contained/normalized; safety authority absent; launch constraints not treated as binding

case_support.signal: foam strike, debris-analysis uncertainty, imagery requests
case_support.failure_mode: program required proof of safety-of-flight issue; foam history normalized

case_support.signal: MCAS hazard assumptions, multiple alerts/indications, pilot-response model
case_support.failure_mode: assumed immediate appropriate human response rather than validating against combined alert conditions

case_support.signal: audits, previous releases, maintenance/investment issues, PSM concerns
case_support.failure_mode: process-safety warnings weakened by cost/production pressure and misleading personal-safety metrics

not_this: not a claim that schedule pressure alone causes disasters
not a claim that managers knowingly chose catastrophe
not a replacement for domain-specific causal analysis
negative_controls_needed: Cases where strong warning signals successfully stopped work/launch/release.
Cases where production pressure existed but did not weaken warning authority.
Cases where warnings were false alarms and were appropriately rejected.
type_payload.query_value: Allows future search for “warnings were given but not authoritative,” across aerospace, aviation, chemical safety, software, finance, medicine, and policy.

positive_controls_needed: Add another official investigation in which pre-event warnings existed and were weakened by authority, schedule, production, certification, or metric pressure.
negative_controls_needed: Add a high-consequence failure with no meaningful pre-event warning signal, to keep the pattern from becoming hindsight bias.
counterexamples_to_seek: Add a case where warning signals did stop operation or force redesign before disaster; this tests what successful warning governance looks like.
rollback_triggers: A second-review extraction demotes or materially weakens one of the support records.
A negative-control record shows the pattern label fits too many unrelated cases.
A counterexample shows the claimed recurrence is better explained by a narrower or different mechanism.
The pattern is upgraded only after controls and not by record count alone.
red_team_controls.split_or_merge_watch: High: proof-burden inversion, normalization, production pressure, certification assumptions, and metric blindness may need child patterns.

maturity_gate.minimum_before_mature: At least one positive control, at least one negative control, an explicit counterexample search, and a rollback/split decision recorded in the claim-status ledger.

handling_notes: Pattern records must not flatten fatal events into management slogans.
Keep burden-of-proof language tied to source-backed record fields, not moral certainty.
When citing this pattern, cite the supporting incident records and their sources.

unknowns: How often does the pattern occur in near-misses rather than disasters?
How should successful warning interventions be encoded?
What source criteria separate hindsight-biased warning detection from genuinely actionable pre-event knowledge?
next_actions: Add a near-miss reporting record from ASRS/CSB/NASA LLIS.
Add theory-source synthesis from Vaughan, Reason, Leveson, Dekker, and process-safety literature.
Split into subpatterns if second-pass review warrants it.
Add at least one negative-control or counterexample record before upgrading this pattern beyond candidate level.
